title: Runtime LTS patch release checklist (v1 working doc)
linked_artifacts: Confluence: ADR-0097 Runtime LTS branching and support window (draft)
Slack: #eng-releases (initial branch cut + RC execution threads)
content:
Doc intent
- This is a working checklist for running an LTS patch release for the serving runtime (kernel + scheduling).
- Informal + pragmatic; the Confluence version will be cleaner later.
- Assumes we have an LTS branch like: runtime-1.20-lts and we’re cutting a patch tag like: runtime-1.20-lts.1

Owners / on-call roles (fill in for each release)
- Release driver (Release Eng): ____________________ (default: Connor O’Brien)
- CI/build captain: ____________________ (default: Sahana Iyer)
- Runtime backport owner: ____________________ (default: Omar El-Sayed)
- Runtime reviewers (kernel/scheduling): ____________________ (e.g., Hiro Tanaka / Sofia Ivanova)
- SRE reliability gate owner (go/no-go): ____________________ (default: Sean Gallagher)
- Security/provenance reviewer (signing/attestation): ____________________ (default: Marcus Lin)
- Audit evidence collector (GRC): ____________________ (default: Olga Petrov)
- Release notes / docs: ____________________ (default: Elliot Price)

Release inputs (must be determined up front)
[ ] Target branch: runtime-____-lts (ex: runtime-1.20-lts)
[ ] Target version/tag: runtime-____-lts.__ (ex: runtime-1.20-lts.1)
[ ] Release type: normal patch | emergency patch (S0/S1)
[ ] Backport freeze time: __________ (date/time + timezone)
[ ] Expected publish time: __________
[ ] Customer comms needed? (Private/Dedicated enterprise) yes/no; list accounts: __________

0) Pre-flight sanity (1–2 business days before RC)
[ ] Confirm branch exists + protection rules in place (no direct pushes; required checks; CODEOWNERS).
    - Notes: branch protection should match PR_8421 intent (LTS-specific required checks + reviewers).
[ ] Confirm LTS backport labels are live + automation is functioning:
    - needs-backport, backport-approved, backport-risk-high (etc)
    - ensure each candidate has a tracking issue (Linear/Jira) and links are present.
[ ] Confirm we have a clean backport queue for this patch:
    - Backport queue tracker updated (risk tier, approvals, conflicts, test evidence, target patch).
    - Identify any “borderline” PRs early (perf refactor-ish changes). Decide now vs during RC.
[ ] Confirm perf baseline + suite version for LTS is stable (benchmark-lab baseline pinned).
[ ] Confirm CI GPU runners capacity for release window (avoid Friday 5pm surprises).
[ ] Confirm private installer + helm chart have support for selecting LTS tags (if this patch needs coordination).
[ ] Decide whether any known issues require explicit callouts / mitigations in notes (check LTS known issues list).

1) Backport intake & approvals (before cutting RC)
For each candidate backport PR:
[ ] Meets LTS eligibility (security / correctness / stability / perf regression fix). Not a feature.
[ ] Has a clear user impact statement (1–3 sentences). If you can’t explain, it’s probably not LTS material.
[ ] Risk tier assigned:
    - LOW: safe bugfix, minimal surface area
    - MED: touches scheduling/kernels but well-contained + test coverage
    - HIGH: wide impact, hard-to-test changes, or perf-sensitive path changes
[ ] Required approvals obtained:
    - Runtime codeowner for touched area (kernel/scheduling)
    - Release Eng approval for process correctness
    - SRE sign-off required for HIGH risk changes (at minimum “aware + plan for canary + rollback”)
[ ] Test evidence attached in PR description/comment:
    - Unit/integration tests
    - Relevant GPU tests
    - Perf-canary link if applicable
[ ] Changelog entry / release-notes snippet drafted (even rough) for each PR.

Cherry-pick mechanics
[ ] Use rw-backport tooling if available; otherwise manual cherry-pick with standardized commit footer:
    - Backport-of: <original SHA>
    - Source-PR: <link>
    - Risk: LOW|MED|HIGH
    - Evidence: <CI links>
[ ] For conflicts: prefer minimal-diff fix; avoid opportunistic cleanup.
[ ] Ensure backport PR title is consistent: "[LTS backport] <original title>"
[ ] Backport PR references release tracking issue (ENG-4821 or patch-specific subtask).

2) Cut release candidate (RC)
[ ] Ensure branch tip is green on required checks BEFORE version bump.
[ ] Create release branch/tag plan:
    - If we do RC tags: runtime-1.20-lts.1-rc.0, rc.1, …
    - If we do RC commits only: document the commit SHA and lock it.
[ ] Bump version (if applicable) on LTS branch.
[ ] Generate provisional changelog for the RC (enterprise-style grouping):
    - Security fixes
    - Correctness & stability
    - Performance
    - Operational changes
    - Known issues / exclusions
[ ] Start audit evidence capture early (don’t wait until publish).

3) CI / build gates (RC must pass all)
Hard gates (no exceptions without explicit SRE + Release Eng sign-off)
[ ] Build reproducibility/determinism check: PASS
    - No unpinned deps; build metadata present; artifact hashes captured.
[ ] LTS CI matrix on supported GPUs: PASS
    - Note which GPU types we’re asserting for this LTS line.
[ ] Runtime unit tests + integration tests: PASS
[ ] E2E smoke on standard inference routes (chat, completion, embeddings if relevant): PASS
[ ] Upgrade/compat checks:
    - confirm no breaking changes to model loading configs expected in Private
    - confirm supported driver/CUDA constraints unchanged (or called out)
[ ] Security/provenance checks: PASS
    - signatures attached
    - provenance/attestation generated
    - “mismatched artifact” protection check (see pipeline race fix work)

Soft gates (must be reviewed; can be waived with explicit note)
[ ] Flaky test summary reviewed and attached to release tracking issue.
[ ] Any CI reruns documented with reason.

4) Perf + reliability gates (SRE-owned go/no-go)
Perf-canary (required for LTS patches; emergency patches may run a shorter canary with explicit waiver)
[ ] Perf-canary run completed against LTS baseline dataset/version.
[ ] Thresholds satisfied (fill values from current policy):
    - p95 latency delta <= ____%
    - p99 latency delta <= ____%
    - throughput delta >= ____% (or <= ____% regression)
[ ] Regression analysis done for any deltas near threshold.

Canary rollout (patch RC)
[ ] Canary duration: ____ hours (min requirement per SRE policy).
[ ] Canary targets:
    - 1 small internal prod slice
    - at least 1 region different from primary
    - at least 1 workload with longer context (if supported)
[ ] Monitors checked during canary:
    - error rate (5xx, timeouts)
    - OOM / memory fragmentation signals
    - queueing / scheduler saturation
    - token throughput / latency distributions
[ ] Rollback criteria agreed + tested path ready.

Go / No-Go decision
[ ] SRE sign-off captured (name + timestamp): __________
[ ] Release Eng sign-off captured (name + timestamp): __________
[ ] Runtime sign-off captured for HIGH risk backports (name + timestamp): __________

5) Artifact publishing (post go)
Where do artifacts go?
- Hosted/Dedicated internal registry: __________
- Private artifacts registry (customer pull): __________
- SBOM/provenance store: __________

Publish steps
[ ] Build final artifacts from approved RC SHA/tag (do NOT rebuild from "latest").
[ ] Verify artifact digests match the signed attestations.
[ ] Push images/binaries to registries with final LTS tag.
[ ] Verify pullability + startup:
    - smoke deploy on a clean environment
    - confirm runtime reports correct version string
[ ] Promote artifact from “staging” to “release” channel (if we have a promotion workflow).
[ ] Update any compatibility metadata consumed by Private installer.

6) Release notes (enterprise format, less noise)
[ ] Create release notes using LTS template (summary + operational impact + risk).
[ ] Required sections (must be present even if "None"):
    - What changed (bullets, grouped)
    - Why it matters (customer-facing)
    - Risk level (overall + per notable change)
    - Behavior changes (including edge-case behavior)
    - Performance deltas (p95/p99 + throughput) + methodology link
    - Known issues + mitigations
    - Upgrade instructions + rollback note
    - Exclusions (explicitly say what we did NOT take)
[ ] Link every bullet to evidence:
    - Source PR
    - backport PR
    - tracking ticket (Linear/Jira)
[ ] Confirm wording is "slower-change" friendly (avoid internal-only refactor chatter).

7) Customer comms / internal comms
Internal
[ ] Post #eng-releases announcement: version, highlights, any caveats, link to notes.
[ ] Post #eng-runtime heads-up if scheduler/kernels changed.
[ ] Post #eng-sre with canary results summary + final go/no-go record.

Customer-facing (only for relevant enterprise accounts)
[ ] Identify accounts requiring proactive notice (Private/Dedicated).
[ ] Send “LTS patch available” email using agreed template:
    - what changed + risk
    - recommended upgrade window
    - rollback guidance
    - support contact / escalation path
[ ] If security fix w/ embargo considerations: coordinate with Security (restricted list; timing; CVE handling).

8) Audit evidence capture (do not skip)
Goal: traceability Issue -> PR -> backport PR -> CI -> artifact digest -> release notes.
[ ] Capture approval evidence:
    - reviewers + sign-offs (screenshots or links)
    - go/no-go decision record
[ ] Capture CI attestations:
    - required checks list + status
    - perf-canary report link
    - canary monitoring screenshots/links
[ ] Capture artifact evidence:
    - image digest(s)
    - SBOM
    - provenance/attestation IDs
    - signing key ID / verification command output
[ ] Store evidence bundle in agreed location and link from release tracking issue.

9) Post-release follow-ups (within 1–3 days)
[ ] Monitor first 24h metrics (errors, latency, restarts, OOMs) on canary + broader rollout.
[ ] Triage any customer tickets referencing this patch; tag as LTS.
[ ] Update "Known issues" living list if something new found.
[ ] Retro (15 min): what broke in the process? update this checklist.

Emergency patch notes (if S0/S1)
- Allowed shortcuts (must be explicitly documented):
  - shorter canary duration (still must canary)
  - release notes may be shorter but must include "why urgent" + rollback
- Not allowed:
  - skipping signing/provenance
  - skipping required CI checks

Common failure modes / reminders (notes to self)
- If a backport PR requires more than 2 conflict-resolution commits, stop and re-evaluate; may be too divergent.
- Avoid "small refactor while I’m here" changes. LTS consumers notice.
- Perf deltas: always compare against LTS baseline, not mainline.
- If CI flakes: document reruns. Auditors and customers both ask.
- If we drop a risky change late: explicitly call it out in release notes (“considered but excluded”).

Appendix: per-release fill-in block (copy/paste)

Branch: runtime-____-lts
Release driver: ____
